title: Toolify3D
claim: Upload an STL file, get a price. No person involved.
heroShotLabel: Hero: the quote screen with an uploaded model and its price
heroCaption: Upload screen showing the model size, volume, material choice, and price.
problem: Quoting by hand on Messenger was slow, and slow quotes lose customers.
The STL file already holds every number a price needs. Nobody was reading it.
built: Three separate services: the shop, the API, and the admin dashboard.
The browser reads the STL file and works out the model's volume. Volume times material density gives the weight, and weight sets the price. The box around the model gives a rough print time.
The shop owner edits the rate table in the admin dashboard. New prices go live at once, with no new deploy.
The browser prices the file so the customer sees a number right away. The server reads the same file again to check that number. A 200k triangle model takes under a second.

images.shotLabel: Upload → quote, price and time visible
images.caption: The quote screen, with weight and print time worked out from the file.
Order states: quoted, accepted, printing, collected.
Material and margin rates, editable without a deploy.

change: Move all file reading to the server, behind a job queue, so the price cannot be faked.
Work out support material from the overhang angles.

title: MediGo
claim: Live matching between patients and doctors. 2nd of 135.
heroShotLabel: Hero: live request being matched on the map
heroCaption: A live patient request with symptoms, a map pin, and the doctors who were called.
problem: A normal doctor list shows who exists. It does not show who is free right now.
Being free has to be live data, not a fixed field in a table.
An unchecked doctor account is a real risk, so identity has to be verified before anyone can take a case.
built: Socket.io tracks each request through its states: open, offered, accepted, withdrawn, closed.
The server sends a request to every on-call doctor inside a radius. The first to accept gets it. If nobody answers, the radius grows.
Matching uses straight-line distance between the patient's GPS point and the doctor's, drawn on an OpenStreetMap layer with Leaflet.
Three roles, guarded by JWT and Supabase row-level security. A new doctor account stays switched off until an admin checks the license number.
The fee is worked out when the case closes: a base rate, raised by how urgent the case is and by the doctor's specialty.
change: Keep live request state in the database, not in server memory.
Use one socket room per district instead of sending to everyone and filtering.
Use road distance or arrival time instead of straight-line distance. A straight line means little in Dhaka traffic.
Move the fee calculation to the server and into a real payment flow. Right now it is only a mock.

title: NBA Cyber-Cell
claim: Harassment reports, sorted and tracked. Built for a national organisation.
heroCaption: The case queue, sorted by urgency, type, and state.
problem: Reports came in as plain messages. There was no shared record to hand over or update.
The women reporting are upset and read Bangla. The form, the advice, and the helpline numbers had to be Bangla from the start, not translated later.
built: The form asks set questions instead of taking free text: type of harassment, platform, when it started, what is known about the person, and any files. A case arrives ready to sort.
Anonymous mode hides the name from staff but still asks for one way to reply, because a report nobody can answer helps nobody.
Every report gets a case ID. The reporter checks status with that ID, with no account and no password left behind on a shared phone.
The admin queue sorts open cases by urgency and state. A safety flag moves a case to the fast path.
File upload with a size limit per file, next to advice to take screenshots before blocking, so the proof is not lost.

images.caption: What the law says, and what steps a reporter can take.

change: Make the case log append-only, and tie each entry to the hash of the one before it. Then an edit to history shows up.
Serve evidence files through signed links that expire, not direct URLs.
Save drafts on the device for people on weak connections.
Rate-limit the form. An open form with no account is also an open door for spam.

title: ByteSpace
claim: Pixel-perfect, animated frontend build. 98+ Lighthouse scores.
heroCaption: The landing page, verified against the Figma design with an automated pixel diff.
problem: The design required a pixel-perfect 1440px implementation that still scaled smoothly down to 375px mobile screens.
Complex UI elements like 3D floating cards and a 'liquid' search button needed to perform well without causing layout shifts or ruining Lighthouse scores.
built: Built a visual-diff script using Playwright and pixelmatch, ensuring the live code remained within 1.87% pixel variance of the original Figma frames.
Scaled complex hero collages purely with CSS math (using `tan(atan2(...))`) so they resize perfectly without relying on JavaScript resize listeners.
Implemented floating 3D shapes using CSS keyframes and a 'goo' SVG filter for the search button, wrapped in a prefers-reduced-motion check for accessibility.
Optimized LCP by fading in the hero headline starting from opacity 0.01 instead of 0, bypassing Chrome's transparent element penalty.

images.caption: Dynamic course filtering and grid layout with accessible focus states.
Swipeable testimonial cards that scale fluidly without JavaScript layout shifts.
Accessible forms with dynamic validation and screen reader announcements.

change: Connect the UI-only authentication forms to a live backend (the hooks are ready).

title: School of Gen Z
claim: Marketing site for an upcoming full-stack Learning Management System.
statusLabel: STATUS: MARKETING LIVE / LMS IN DEV
heroShotLabel: Hero: School of Gen Z landing page
heroCaption: The live marketing site showcasing upcoming courses and platform features.
problem: The brand needed an immediate public presence to attract students and build interest while the complex backend of the LMS is actively being built.
The architecture requires a seamless transition from a fast, static marketing funnel into a secure, dynamic student portal.
built: A responsive marketing frontend built in React and deployed on Vercel to establish the brand identity and outline the course catalog.
Currently architecting the underlying MERN stack backend (MongoDB, Express, Node.js) to support distinct user roles (admin, instructor, student).
Designing the database schema for course enrollment, video module progress tracking, and secure authentication.

images.caption: Marketing view of the upcoming learning tracks.
Highlighting the tools and resources for students.

change: Launch the interactive student dashboard and video module player.
Connect the frontend to the Node.js API to enable live user registration, secure login, and course enrollment.

title: RedLife
claim: A national blood donation network for Bangladesh. Live donor matching.
heroShotLabel: Hero: RedLife dashboard and request board
heroCaption: The live donation request board connecting patients with active donors.
problem: Finding blood donors in an emergency requires filtering by exact blood group across all 64 districts and 490+ upazilas in Bangladesh.
A flat list isn't enough; the platform needs a triaged workflow (pending, in progress, done) managed by volunteers and admins.
built: A role-based dashboard (Donor, Volunteer, Admin) where every new user is an active donor, and admins control the status of live requests.
Separated the architecture into a Next.js 16 App Router frontend and an Express API backend, secured with Better Auth sessions and short-lived JWTs.
Built a donor search tool that filters by exact location and exports the results directly to a downloadable PDF using jspdf.
Integrated Stripe Checkout in test mode to accept funding contributions, tracked via an admin stat dashboard.

images.caption: The live donation request board connecting patients with active donors.
Donor dashboard tracking personal donation history and status.
Integrated Stripe Checkout for platform contributions.
Charts and metrics tracking donors, funding, and daily requests.

change: Implement SMS notifications so donors get pinged instantly when an urgent request matches their district and blood type.

title: Kitbash
claim: Neo-brutalist marketplace for design and dev kits. Buy, remix, ship.
meta: NEXT.JS 16 · REACT 19 · TAILWIND V4 · GSAP · FIREBASE
heroShotLabel: Hero: Kitbash landing page with the interactive kit stage
heroCaption: The hero kit card, with live theme swatches.
problem: Makers lose days on blank canvases. They need ready kits they can ship fast.
Marketplaces look bland and alike. This one needed a bold identity.
built: Catalog with category chips, search, price filter, and sorting.
Seller Studio with a live card preview that updates as you type.
Firebase Auth (Google and email) with Firestore for user kits.
Neo-brutalist system: 3px borders, hard shadows, GSAP motion.

Publish form beside a live preview.
Closing section pushing makers to browse or publish.
